subject.title: fix(zalo): add timeouts to Bot API requests

question: Should ordinary Zalo Bot API operations use a fixed 30-second client deadline by default, including potentially slower send/media and webhook operations?
rationale: The code correctly implements the stated behavior, but choosing a new default availability ceiling trades indefinite hangs for possible failure of slow valid operations and is a plugin behavior policy decision.

options.title: Accept the 30-second default
options.body: Keep the proposed default for all ordinary API calls, with explicit call-site overrides remaining available for operations that require a longer deadline.

options.title: Narrow the deadline scope
options.body: Apply the default only to selected control-plane calls or introduce explicit per-operation timeouts where slow uploads and response bodies need different limits.

options.title: Pause for operational evidence
options.body: Wait for owner guidance or production-like Zalo timing evidence before adopting a global ordinary-call deadline.

recommendation.title: Accept the 30-second default
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed default for all ordinary API calls, with explicit call-site overrides remaining available for operations that require a longer deadline.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Zalo abort-handling work makes them the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate available in the supplied history.
